content:
This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will officially launch to all users on Monday, September 14.

In addition, the company now says that two features included in the iOS 27 beta have been removed and will instead arrive in a 'future software update' for iPhones: suggested features in Messages, and the ability to automatically change passwords.

Apple updated its website this week to reflect that it has now pulled these features from iOS 27. The change applies to other platforms as well, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users had previously spotted that the auto-change password feature was removed in the fifth iOS 27 beta, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm the change.

As a refresher, the suggested features in the Messages app allow users to add items to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with just a tap, based on the content of their conversations.

Here's how Apple described the Passwords feature:

The Passwords app will try to navigate directly to sites where you're using weak or leaked passwords and automatically update them. At WWDC, Apple explained that the feature uses Apple Intelligence and Safari to 'agentically take action on your behalf.'

There are no further details on when these two features will return in iOS 27. Apple's website simply states that they will appear in a 'future software update.'
